newsitem.title: USA: Hearing planned for Milwaukee stadium bill.
newsitem.headline: Hearing planned for Milwaukee stadium bill.

text.p: A Wisconsin Senate committee has scheduled a hearing for Wednesday on a proposal to cap the use of local sales tax revenues for the new ballpark for the Milwaukee Brewers American League baseball team.

The bill would set a $160 million bond limit for the stadium's oversight board, Southeast Wisconsin Professional Baseball Park District, and prohibit the use of sales tax revenues to make lease payments for stadium costs.
The Senate Judiciary Committee hearing is scheduled for Wednesday afternoon, according to an aide to committee chairman Sen. Lynn Adelman, D-New Berlin.
District officials have called the bill unconstitutional and said it could kill the $250 million project if it passes.
The bill passed a Senate economic development committee in March, but was moved to the judiciary committee after questions about its legality were raised.
The district on March 5 sold $146.7 million of tax-exempt, sales tax revenue bonds backed by a 0.1 percent, five-county sales tax and insured by MBIA Insurance Corp.

Statements in the preliminary official statement for that deal outlined the possibility that another $45 million of parity bonds could be issued to pay for stadium equipment, leading to the introduction of the bill by Sen. Joe Wineke, D-Verona.
